in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with the basics: **Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have one child, Alex, who is 11 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know that you have Alex, who is 11 years old and lives with you.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I need to ask: **Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand a bit more about Alex's situation.

**Is Alex in any of the following circumstances:**
- Currently in hospital or care?
- Living with someone else (even temporarily)?
- Working for 24 hours or more per week?
- Receiving any benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply to Alex. He lives with me full-time, isn't in hospital or care, doesn't work, and doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another relative?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that, actually. I don't know if anyone else is claiming for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. That's an important detail because only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at any given time.

Let me ask this differently: **Are you Alex's parent, and if so, does Alex have another parent who might be claiming Child Benefit for him?** Or if you're not the parent, what is your relationship to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am Alex's parent. As for whether his other parent is claiming Child Benefit for him, I honestly don't know. We haven't discussed it, so I'm not sure if they're claiming or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since you're Alex's parent and he lives with you full-time, that's helpful information.

Let me ask one more important question: **Are you responsible for Alex's upkeep?** In other words, do you provide for his day-to-day needs such as food, clothes, accommodation, and other living expenses?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I provide for all of Alex's day-to-day needs - his food, clothes, accommodation, everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! Based on the information you've provided, you are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 11 years old (under 16), meeting the age requirement
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you full-time
- You're responsible for all of Alex's day-to-day needs
- Alex is not in any circumstances that would prevent a claim (hospital, care, working, or receiving benefits)

**Important point to note:** Only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child. Since you're unsure whether Alex's other parent is currently claiming, you should check this before applying. If they are claiming and you want to claim instead, you would need to agree between yourselves who will receive it. If you cannot agree, HMRC will decide.

**What to do next:** If you're not already claiming and want to apply, you can make a claim for Child Benefit. If it turns out that someone else is already claiming for Alex, HMRC will contact you to help resolve the situation.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
